- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) — reduce initial forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >85) — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.3) or shows negative momentum (e.g., -0.33, 0.00), reduce forecast by 5–10% and apply downward bias to next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if recent 3-day trend is upward.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), forecast should be closer to historical mean (last 10–15 days) — avoid extrapolation.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent overestimation — apply exponential decay weighting (e.g., 0.95 decay per day) to reduce long-term bias.
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over 3+ days, forecast should be capped at 10–15% below recent peak to avoid “overbought” mispricing.
